quotesThemes: If anyone would be disqualified, Ord would be the one.
A full phylactery would have been a full fire; the smolder means trace soul magic and maybe more enchantments.
What you have here is definitely not a phylactery.

notes: Asked in Draconic whether Walker has changed since wearing the helm, she starts to answer Dana, then clamps her mouth around Walker's head by the helm and lifts him. The bite hurts her.
Through the mind link she tells him to give up the helmet, asks whether phylacteries are flame resistant, and offers to torch it.

She says he seems influenced and that she cannot diagnose mind control. She then tells Dana he has not acted any stranger than normal, and that she still wants to light him on fire to see if it burns. She says he will be fine.
She knows Walker's internal fire can spread and protect her through the bond.
She lands in the street by Carlkin's lighthouse beside Araden. Carlkin distinguishes the larger copper, Araden, from Glimmen.
Walker says that if Grixto is influencing either of them, it would be Glimmen. He counts her voice among the familiar voices that would not count as Carlkin's warning sign.
personality: Blunt with Walker about the helm, and willing to manhandle him or burn the helm to force a test.
quotesThemes: Walker, just give him the helmet.
Do you think phylacteries are flame resistant?
Well he hasn't acted any stranger than normal. I think I should still light him on fire and see if it burns.

Grixto.existing: The emperor Walker killed, a lich hiding a phylactery among mundane possessions or chess pieces.
notes: Finding him remains one of Sylan's stated priorities, alongside freeing Sylan's sister, before the party detours into the ghost investigation.

Walker knows him as the emperor: a hobgoblin in purple robes. Walker killed him, then spoke with him after picking up the helm. He seemed different. The conversation was calm and respectful, not frightening.

He called the golden fire of Walker's gold dragon rider bond Walker's life force, and said that energy is as significant to him as it is to Walker. He wants people to rule as they did before the Voyager gods.

Walker names him as the one who might be influencing Walker or Glimmen. The party says he has contacted them twice from wherever he is. Dana suspected the helm, which Walker carried the whole time, could explain that contact.
Carlkin treats the helm as the item this lich was wearing when he died. Only a tiny imprint remains. The helm itself is not the phylactery.
Sylan warns that if he senses his phylactery destroyed he can make another before they find him. Walker wants a phylactery destroyed only when they have eyes on its owner.
Walker hopes the helm's soul fragment can be used to track him. That question is unanswered, and Sylan is not at the lighthouse to help.
personality: In the helm conversation he was calm, respectful, and concerned with rule as it was before the Voyager gods.
quotesThemes: The golden fire of the gold dragon rider bond is Walker's life force, and that energy is as significant to him as it is to Walker.
People should rule as they did before the Voyager gods.
openQuestions: How has he contacted the party, now that the helm has been ruled out as his phylactery?
Can the helm's soul fragment lead the party back to him?

notes: He looks vaguely half-elf and stands about 5'10" to 5'11". His ancient copper dragon is Araden. Gerk knew about the dragon and had not known this height.
He has been training Walker in meditation and introduces him to Benji as his new recruit. He and Araden had met the party at the council of the gods, but had not met Benji with them.

Hearing that Gerk needs more door training, he says that makes two of them and offers to train Gerk. He tells the party to have the helm investigated, then return to Walker's training. He pokes Gerk in the midriff.
He says Gerk is strong of body and lacking in mind, compares him to an oak sapling, and says the growth he means is mental. He addresses him as "my boy."
He follows with Araden as the Carlkin group leaves the forest. Araden sets him down at Carlkin's door. He greets Benji with a cordial embrace.
The accounts disagree about the age remark: one has Elrus saying Benji looks old for his age and asking whether he has been meditating; the other has Benji saying that of Elrus.
personality: Speaks to Gerk as a student, calls him "my boy," and frames the criticism of his mind as cultivation rather than an insult.
quotesThemes: You seem to be strong of body, but your mind seems to be lacking. We will work that out of you.
It is not an insult, my boy. One does not insult an oak tree as a sapling. They just know one day it'll be more.
Not pick in here, but pick in there, your mind, boy.
Walker needs some help meditating.
I've been training my new recruit. There he is, Walker.

Ciri.existing: Half-elf rogue and Gatekeeper of Lith.
notes: She agrees Walker's fire-resistance claim should be tested and starts a tinderbox under his arm.
She goes to Carlkin's with Walker, Dana, and Ord. She cannot ride Dana's broom. Araden carries her on the flight.

Doorway.existing: Gerk's fixed supernatural passage between locations.
notes: Recent training lets Gerk manipulate doors a little better. He still needs practice. Elrus is willing to train him.
Doors open into the abyss, and giant monsters come out, when Gerk thinks about nothing. He distinguishes that from simply failing to be quiet. Dana says doorway focus is separate from rage.
He expects raging while opening a door to go poorly. The seventeen-foot door was an attempt to open it harder. Sylan wants him to try rage at the next training.
Dana forbids doors to nothing dimensions, abyssal monsters, and doors opened in moving vehicles.

Yesterday's door at Carlkin's commons was extradimensional, which Gerk says he did not intend. His other doors were interdimensional. Haldor now bars both extradimensional and interdimensional doors inside New Navel and points the practice to the forest.
Sylan says the sword lets him travel to another place where he can see spirits. He enters it before going down the vale and does not think that should be done in the open.

Inside is a gray spirit field, distinct from the Abyssal Plane. Sylan becomes ghostly and translucent there, so physical objects pass through him. Gerk sees him as foggy. Returning leaves rocks on his feet.

It is emptier than on earlier visits. The giant who had been inside was released. Sylan does not think he is holding anyone else. Distant figures can still be seen, and a prayer with Arcana 21 lets him pull specific spirits toward himself.
He calls it a bad place to leave spirits. The pull brings the raven emissary, who stops him from reclaiming spirits he had already sent on.
Haldor knows the sword as the one that looks large because Sylan is small.

Shades and Trades.existing: Where Sylan found the staff later fused to Ord's lantern.
notes: The shop is in the middle of New Navel. Sylan plans to bring the fused lantern-staff here to identify it, and he is unsure whether the party already did that. He does not go there first.

He first treats the proprietor as a living human, then decides the proprietor was a ghost. He has been around that proprietor before and has not taken him. He holds off on entering because of where the shop sits, then plans to reach it by the long way through town so he does not miss anyone.
openQuestions: Is the proprietor a spirit, and if so, why did Sylan's proximity not take him?

Araden.existing: A magically capable companion brought secretly to The Reach.
notes: She is Elrus's ancient copper dragon, large enough that landing in New Navel means curling her wings and keeping her tail off the roofs. Dana identifies her as the dragon of the rider mentoring Walker, not as Glimmen.
She flies Elrus and the Carlkin group to the lighthouse, carries Ciri, and is also described as carrying Ord. She sets Elrus down at Carlkin's door.
She tells Ciri, "Don't worry, little one. I will carry you." She tells Ord not to worry, addresses him as young Lane, taps his chest, and says his wings are in there.
Carlkin already knows her and is put out that nobody told him she had been brought. She visibly perks up when Benji comes toward her. Glimmen lands beside her.
She flies faster than an average ship. Carlkin says entering the Sunder Chase with her would now be cheating and would get a rider disqualified.
Walker counts her voice among the familiar voices that would not count as Carlkin's possession warning.
quotesThemes: Don't worry, little one. I will carry you.
Don't worry, young Lane. Your wings are in here.

Dana's magic broom.existing: Magic broom from the white dragon hoard, flying 50 feet.
notes: It cannot take a passenger. Dana treats the limit as a weight limit, or a weight limit on speed. Ciri cannot ride it to the lighthouse.

Named only in the morning recap: Barker might have made a deal with Vecna, mentioned alongside a concerning sister-skin journal. The hearing of the name is uncertain. No further detail appears in these scenes.
openQuestions: Did Barker make a deal with Vecna? The name itself was uncertain in the recap.

notes: Appears in Sylan's gray sword-realm while he prays and draws the distant figures in. A flicker in the gray sky becomes a raven hovering two or three feet from his face. It studies him after he nods, then becomes a middle-aged person sized between a halfling and a dwarf, read as a thin or anemic dwarf or a very muscular halfling, draped in feathers.
The figure makes the same noise as on an earlier visit, then speaks. No name is given.

He calls Sylan Razor, says the spirits were not attached and that Sylan already sent them on, and asks why Sylan pulls them back. He names Sylan Raven's razor and the pathway to the falls, and begins the duty to seek certain souls before the line is lost.
Told that the spirits had things left, he says they did, but she will say. He checks that Sylan is not pulling more back. Sylan stops.
personality: Direct and corrective. He stops Sylan from reclaiming spirits who were already sent on and points the unanswered business back to the Raven Queen.
quotesThemes: What are you doing, Razor?
They were not attached to you. You have sent them on their way. Why do you pull them back?
You are Raven's razor. You are the pathway to the falls.
You are a razor of the Raven Queen. It is your duty to seek out those who…
They did, but she will say.

Raven Queen.existing: Elder god of death, also called Nira, who once walked among mortals and can take a harpy-like form.
notes: Her emissary names Sylan a razor of the Raven Queen, with a duty to seek certain dead and to serve as the pathway to the falls. The specific charge is cut off.
Spirits who claimed unfinished business are deferred to her: they did have things left, but she will say.
Sylan says she cannot be cheated at the end of a life's allotment.
Sylan tells Haldor he serves her as a cleric, assigned to find people who escaped their end and send them on. Haldor does not know the gods and does not pick up the theology.

Everfalls.existing: A location from the party's past where the Raven Queen has seen both Sylan and Dana.
notes: The raven emissary calls Sylan the pathway to the falls while naming him Raven's razor.

Benji.existing: Familiar with The Reach and may be at the party's bar.
notes: He is a warforged. The party already heard that explanation in The Reach, and he was with them when they finished the Sunder Chase. He had not yet met Elrus and Araden together with the party.
He is inside Carlkin's lighthouse, pushes past Dana, and goes straight to Araden, who perks up. He and Elrus embrace.
He and Carlkin have known each other since about the time the Sunder Chase started. Benji claims he gave Carlkin the idea. He defends the other copper dragon when Carlkin calls that dragon a fool.
The age-and-meditation remark between him and Elrus is inconsistent across accounts about which of them said the other looks old.
personality: Quick to claim the Sunder Chase idea and to defend the other copper dragon.

notes: Carlkin calls it a death race. Carlkin and Benji trace their friendship, and the argument over who had the idea, to when it first started. Benji claims he gave Carlkin the idea.

The party won it. Carlkin says he gave them some guidance. Ord's contribution was dispelling magic on another ship. Typical tactics are cannons, faster sails, or burning ships. A dragon simply flying faster than a ship is the other route.

Riding Araden is now considered cheating and would disqualify a rider. Araden flies faster than an average ship. Another copper dragon, still around and distinct from Araden, is now a hoard dragon for the race.

Hanzuni.existing: Ancient copper dragon of Haven Hold who loans gold for quests.
notes: Not named in these scenes. Carlkin and Benji discuss another copper dragon, distinct from Araden, who is still present and is now a hoard dragon for the Sunder Chase. Carlkin calls that dragon a fool. Benji objects. The transcript renders the epithet unclear, heard as something like "inspiratory dragon."
openQuestions: Was the unnamed hoard dragon actually Hanzuni? The name was not spoken.

notes: Sheriff of New Navel. Gerk later refers to him as Howdy. His house is southwest of the market, down the road and to the right, past and behind the tavern.

Gerk finds him on the porch in a rocking chair, boots up on a stump, hands folded, hat brim low. He was resting, and he had been after a cutpurse. He recognizes Gerk, has not seen him in some time, and agrees to walk outside the gate and hear the spirit problem. He shakes Sylan's hand.

He knows Sylan as Gerk's short elven friend, whose sword looks large because Sylan is small. He says Sylan has not been sucking up spirits before, treats it as a change, and confirms Sylan has not pulled in any of the party.

He enforces the ban on extradimensional doors inside the city limits and is unfamiliar with Gerk's interdimensional-versus-extradimensional distinction. He then states the stricter rule, citing a posted change: both extradimensional and interdimensional doors are prohibited in the city, magic practice goes to the forest, and spirit-taking is not permitted. He hoped Gerk was carrying interdimensional shackles and refuses a door opened to fetch them.

He will not investigate a portal opened in someone's house. Carlkin already reported the commons portal, which Haldor calls a hell portal and a tentacle-spewing portal, and reported that Gerk fixed the floor. Haldor has charges he has not interpreted. He files the party as stronghold hooligans, says most of that file is Carlkin, and would rather wait a day or two for the party to leave than walk to the stronghold.

He bet Erwin 25 gold that the Trigash beacon was a random event and not the party. Erwin said it was hooligans flying that way with a new dragon. Haldor lost. Erwin saw them fly toward the forest and back about an hour later. The fliers were in town about forty-five minutes before this conversation.

He knows Joanna's wicker animals, says her geese are good, and describes the goose-seller two doors down as a decent vendor who keeps a flock in cages. He tells Gerk not to threaten villagers. He shuts down the windows joke.

He remembers Ledzbika's rants, his death about a month ago from natural causes, and that the neighbor was trying to steal his belongings. Ledzbika did not return as a ghost or echo, which Haldor calls the puzzle. He has no recent missing-persons cases. He estimates a handful to maybe a dozen deaths in six or seven months, plus travelers.

He calls returned town dead celestial echoes, distinct from undead. Spirits fall under undead. Summoning undead is illegal, and he will confiscate the lantern if it is not kept hidden. His Neville prison-and-echo account is secondhand and shaky, loosely tied to a sea-associated elder god. He says he knows nothing about the gods.

He says the mines across the lake are opening again, with greater competition and more people coming and going. He wants to know how long the party will remain. Told that they will eat, plan, and leave soon, and that nothing further is needed from him, he parts on good terms if they keep Gerk's dragon friend away from the ghosts, open no doors in town, and keep commotion outside town.
Gerk understands him as having ordered Gerk to stay out of town.
personality: Unhurried and at ease on his own porch, familiar and dry with Gerk.
Prefers less paperwork and would rather wait out the party than walk to the stronghold.
Firm about city limits, vendors, doors, and keeping trouble outside town.
Says he knows nothing about the gods and does not trust the echo story as a fully sober account.
quotesThemes: I just label it stronghold hooligans.
If I wait a day or so you'll be gone anyway, so it's less paperwork for me.
I don't know nothing about no gods.
Extra-dimensional and interdimensional doors are now prohibited within the city limits.
Spirit sucking is not permitted, and summoning undead is against town rules.
They are not ghosts here; they are echoes. Echoes are celestials, undead are undead, and spirits fall under undead.
We escaped Neville not realizing we were in a prison of sorts.
No doors. Have your friends open it for you.
openQuestions: What charges did Carlkin file? Haldor has not had time to read them.

Carlkin's lighthouse.existing: Carlkin's lighthouse in New Navel is his home and bookshop, where an abyss door opens onto a fight with tentacles and a wall of eyes.
notes: The study floor is still a mess a day after the doorway. The center looks like a sandbox shoved up through the flagstones.
A corner holds a small desk and study setup, including an altar-like lectern where Walker leaves the helm.
Carlkin answers only after a crate slides, a chain rattles, and metal rasps. Dragons landing nearby draw a stir in the streets.
Walker wears a golden glove and uses that hand, together with his fire resistance, to pull the helm out of Carlkin's burning bag. The heat comes to basically nothing.
A small basket-woven wicker chicken Gerk buys from Joanna in the New Navel market for one gold. He carries it to Haldor's porch and shows it to Sylan, who judges it well crafted.
Gerk says it has uses and that he has not killed the wicker creatures yet. The same stall had a near life-size wicker goose, which he does not take.
Living vendor in the New Navel market. She sells wicker animals, including a small wicker chicken and a one-to-one wicker goose, and says she can make geese or a gander.
Gerk pays her one gold for the chicken. She gives him directions to Haldor's house. Haldor recognizes the chicken as hers and says she makes good geese.
personality: Friendly, and eager to sell a goose after the chicken.

notes: Two doors down from Joanna. Sells nothing but geese and keeps a flock in cages.
Haldor calls him a decent vendor and tells Gerk not to threaten villagers. Gerk points at him, says he will be back, and later admits he threatened him, mostly in jest.
In New Navel when the Trigash beacon went up. He bet Haldor 25 gold that it was the stronghold hooligans rather than a random event. Haldor lost and owes him the money.
He saw a bunch of the party fly toward the forest with a new dragon in tow, then fly back about an hour later. He is not present for the later conversation.

Trigash Forest.existing: Forest outskirts where a beacon rose and spirits stayed back.
notes: A couple of miles from New Navel, over yonder from the gate. Haldor identifies it as the place of the day's midmorning beacon, the blinding, and the spirits entering Sylan.
From town the beacon was a giant column of light. Erwin watched the party fly in with a dragon and fly back about an hour later. Gerk and Sylan walked back. The others flew.
Haldor tells Gerk to practice doorway magic out there because doors are banned in the city. Gerk had already practiced doors that day in a clearing away from people.
Haldor asks whether Gerk has them and hoped to use them on the spirit problem. Gerk does not. Haldor refuses Gerk's offer to open a doorway to a set of shackles inside the city.

newTerms.name: Golden eagle
notes: Token Walker has from his meeting with Vecna, the god of the undead. Vecna tapped it on a table; Walker took the gesture for boredom, and Dana treats it as a hint toward the phylactery. Distinct from the helm.
Placed on the war table, it lights the map. Walker thinks it is one half of a pair, with the match at Vecna's Nyx palace.

newTerms.name: War table
notes: Map table that lights up when the golden eagle is placed on it. Walker thinks they need to find it, or put this piece on the one they already know.

newTerms.name: Elrus's ancient copper dragon
notes: Unnamed ancient copper-colored dragon with Elrus during this conversation. Gerk already knew Elrus had an ancient dragon.

newTerms.name: Sylan's sword
notes: Lets Sylan travel to a place where he can see spirits. He wants to check it and remove any spirits before going down the vale, because it is a bad place for them.

newTerms.name: Sylan's sword-realm
notes: Gray, rolling spirit field reached through Sylan's sword. It is not the Abyssal Plane. He turns translucent there, can see spirits, and can try to draw distant figures to him.
Emptier than on past visits. The giant once held there has been released. Sylan calls it a bad place.

newTerms.name: Unnamed raven figure
notes: A raven that interrupts Sylan's summoning in the sword-realm and turns into a feather-draped, middle-aged person built between a halfling and a dwarf. Unnamed. This emissary gives Sylan the title Raven's Razor.

newTerms.name: Raven's Razor
notes: Title the feathered emissary gives Sylan. Also called the pathway to the falls. A razor of the Raven Queen seeks souls who will not move on when their allotment ends. Distinct from Talon.
The pathway-to-the-falls name may connect to Everfalls, but that link is unexplained.

newTerms.name: Walker's golden glove
notes: Glove Walker is wearing. With his fire resistance, he uses it to pull the helm from Carlkin's burning bag.

newTerms.name: Carlkin's soul-cleaning bag
notes: A bag of holding Carlkin enchanted to detect phylactery soul magic and ignite on contact. The helm only made it smolder, and the bag then burned away.

newTerms.name: Emperor
notes: Carlkin's name for the person Walker took the white helm from. Walker killed him and then spoke with him; Walker says he was different. Carlkin links that contact to the spiritual attachment on the helm. No other identity is given.

newTerms.name: Haldor
notes: Sheriff of New Navel. Lives just past the tavern, southwest of the market. Gerk finds him relaxed on his porch.
Keeps the party file he calls stronghold hooligans. Gerk fetches him about the spirits in Sylan; he walks Gerk out to question Sylan and explains celestial echoes.
Enforces the bans on interdimensional doors, spirit-sucking, summoning undead, and town commotion. Wants Gerk's dragon kept away from the ghosts.

newTerms.name: Wicker chicken
notes: Small woven chicken Gerk buys from Joanna in the New Navel market for one gold. She also sells wicker geese.

newTerms.name: Joanna
notes: New Navel market vendor who weaves wicker chickens and geese. She directs Gerk to Haldor's house. Haldor names her as the source of Gerk's chicken and says she makes good geese.

newTerms.name: Stronghold hooligans
notes: Haldor's label for the shared sheriff's file on the party. He says most of it comes from Carlkin. Erwin uses the same name for the Trigash beacon bet.

newTerms.name: Spirit jug
notes: Haldor and Gerk's name for Sylan taking bad spirits in so they can be sent home. Haldor treats this as new and writes that it is not permitted.

newTerms.name: Erwin
notes: Someone in New Navel who saw the Trigash beacon and the party flying that way with a dragon. He bet they were the stronghold hooligans with a new dragon, and Haldor owes him 25 gold.

newTerms.name: Interdimensional shackles
notes: Restraints Haldor hoped Gerk was carrying for the spirit incident. Gerk does not have them.

newTerms.name: Celestial echo
notes: A celestial copy of a dead resident or traveler of New Navel, from when the town was Neville. At death they could choose this instead of passing on. Distinct from ghosts, undead, and spirits.

newTerms.name: Soul identifier
notes: Carlkin's clear two-to-three-ounce reagent, shaken from a brackish mix, used to read an item more closely than the bag. On the helm a drop beads and sticks instead of running off, showing a spiritual attachment.

newTerms.name: Golden fire
notes: Walker's gold dragon rider bond. The emperor treated it as Walker's life force.
